描述_ZN: Kong Envy Monument" is also known as "Wei Lu Confucius Temple Monument" and "Kong Envy Repairing Confucius Temple Monument". It was erected in the first year of the Huangchu period (220) of the Wei Dynasty of the Three Kingdoms. The tablet is now placed in the Tongwen Gate of the Confucius Temple in Qufu, Shandong Province. The topography of the tablet is 188 cm long and 84 cm wide, in clerical script, with 22 lines and 40 characters. The frontispiece is inscribed in seal script with six characters, "The Tablet of the Temple of Confucius in Lu". On the left side of the stele is an inscription inscribed by Zhang Zhigui in the seventh year of the Song Dynasty (1062), which is said to be written by Liang Kuangshu, but there is no evidence. This stele records that Wei made Kong Xian, the twenty-first grandson of Confucius, the marquis of Zongsheng and dedicated to Confucius, and repaired the temple of Confucius and set up guards to guard it.　　The style of this stele is strong, cold and thrifty, dense and majestic, and is representative of the Wei script. Hong Shih in the "official interpretation" that "Wei Li can be treasured four stele, this is the crown." Zhao Life in "Graphite Engraving" cloud: "This stele is ancient and robust."　　The Ming topography of the stele is in the collection of the Forbidden City. The ink is very fine, in which the word "body" survives next to the word "qu", and the word "said Chong" is already connected. The upper left corner of the word "zai" is lost. It is signed by Zhu Yi container.　　The "Kong Envy Tablet" is recorded in Zhao Mingcheng's "Jin Shi Lu" in the Song Dynasty, Gu Yanwu's "Jin Shi Wen Ji" in the Qing Dynasty, and Weng Fang Gang's "Jin Shi Ji of the Two Han Dynasties" and other books.
